Rashi on Shabbat 95b:1:1.hebrew: אלא להכשיר זרעים - הזרועים בתוכו. עציץ נקוב אינו מקבל הכשר לטומאה, ושאינו נקוב מקבל הכשר, דתלוש הוא. והא רבי שמעון קאמר ליה, וה"ג: ר"ש אומר אין בין נקוב כו'. דאילו לרבנן איכא טובא, דהא מיחייבי אנקוב משום שבת, ופטרי אשאינו נקוב:
Rashi on Shabbat 95b:1:1.english: Except to render seeds [susceptible] - [Those] that are sown in it. A perforated pot does not receive susceptibility to ritual impurity, whereas an imperforated [pot] receives susceptibility, because it is [considered] detached. And this [statement] is [what] Rabbi Shimon said, and thus is the reading: "Rabbi Shimon says: There is no [difference] between a perforated [pot], etc." For according to the Rabbis there are many [differences], since they hold [one] liable for a perforated [pot] on account of Shabbat, and exempt [one] for an imperforated [pot].

Rashi on Shabbat 95b:1:2.hebrew: לכל מילי - לשבת, ולקנות במשיכה ולא בכסף, ולפרוזבול שאינו נכתב אלא על הקרקע:
Rashi on Shabbat 95b:1:2.english: For all matters - For Shabbat, and for acquiring [it] through pulling (meshikhah) and not through money, and for a prozbul, which is only written on land.

Rashi on Shabbat 95b:1:3.hebrew: אשר יזרע - כדרך שאדם מוציא לזריעה, למעוטי מחובר כל דהו. להכי אהני זריעות יתירי דקרא, ומיהו שאינו נקוב תלוש גמור הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 95b:1:3.english: That is sown - In the manner that a person takes [seed] out for sowing, to exclude [from impurity] anything that is attached [to the ground] in any way. For this [purpose] the extra [mentions of] sowing in the verse are effective, however, an imperforated [pot] is [considered] completely detached.

Rashi on Shabbat 95b:2:1.hebrew: מה לי אמר רבי שמעון - מי מודה, דהא במחובר הוא האי שורש, ואי תלשו לי' בשבת מיחייב:
Rashi on Shabbat 95b:2:1.english: What would Rabbi Shimon say - Does he concede that this root is [considered] attached [to the ground], and if one plucks it on Shabbat, he is liable?

Rashi on Shabbat 95b:2:3.hebrew: שאם ניקב - העציץ בכדי טהרתו, ושאם נטמא נטהר בשבירה זו. והיינו כמוציא זית, דתנן במסכת כלים (פ"ג מ"א): כלי חרס העשוי לאוכלין שיעורו כזיתים. ומודה ר' שמעון בהא דחשיב מחובר כל הזרעים שבתוכו, דתו לא הוי כלי:
Rashi on Shabbat 95b:2:3.english: That if it was perforated - [if] the flowerpot [was perforated] enough to render it ritually pure, meaning that if it had become ritually impure it would become pure through this breakage. And this is [a hole large enough] to let an olive pass through, as we learned in Tractate Kelim (3:1): "An earthenware vessel made for foods — its measure [for becoming pure] is [the size of] olives." And Rabbi Shimon agrees in this [case] that all the seeds inside it are considered attached [to the ground], since it is no longer a vessel.

Rashi on Shabbat 95b:2:4.hebrew: ניקב בכדי טהרתו מיבעיא - דהוה לן לספוקי ביה בהנך דלאו כנגד הנקב, ואת פשטת להו דכולהו מחובר נינהו:
Rashi on Shabbat 95b:2:4.english: [If] it is perforated to the measure of its purity, is there a question - For we should have been in doubt regarding it — regarding those [roots] that are not opposite the hole — and [yet] you resolved [the doubt regarding] them, [ruling] that all of them are [considered] attached.

Rashi on Shabbat 95b:3:1.hebrew: אי אתמר לדרבי זירא - דמודה ר"ש בשום נקב:
Rashi on Shabbat 95b:3:1.english: If [that] of Rabbi Zeira was stated - that Rabbi Shimon agrees regarding any perforation.

Rashi on Shabbat 95b:3:2.hebrew: הכי הוא דאיתמר - שאם ניקב למטה מרביעית, שאינו מחזיק רביעית מן הנקב ולמטה, דבציר מהכי לאו כלי הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 95b:3:2.english: It was stated as follows - That if it was perforated below a quarter [of a log], [meaning] that it does not hold a quarter [of a log] from the hole and below, for less than this is not a vessel.

Rashi on Shabbat 95b:4:10.hebrew: טהור מלהכשיר זרעים - לרבנן, דהוי עציץ נקוב:
Rashi on Shabbat 95b:4:10.english: It is ritually pure from rendering seeds capable [of contracting impurity] - According to the Rabbis, for it is [considered] a perforated flowerpot.

Rashi on Shabbat 95b:4:11.hebrew: ועדיין כלי הוא לקבל בו זיתים - שהוא שיעור לטומאה בכל כלי חרס העשוי לאוכלין סתם, כל זמן שלא יחדו לרימונים, ומקבל עדיין טומאה:
Rashi on Shabbat 95b:4:11.english: And it is still a vessel to hold olives in it - For [that] is the measure for ritual impurity in any earthenware vessel made for food in general, as long as one has not designated it for pomegranates, and it still contracts ritual impurity.

Rashi on Shabbat 95b:4:12.hebrew: טהור מלקבל בו זיתים - כלומר, מלקבל עוד טומאה משום תורת סתם כלי חרס, שהרי שיעורן כזיתים. ואם היתה עליו טומאה, נטהר ממנה:
Rashi on Shabbat 95b:4:12.english: Pure from holding olives in it - That is to say, [it is pure] from further contracting impurity under the law of an ordinary earthenware vessel, since their [standard] measure is [the size of] olives. And if impurity was [already] upon it, it becomes purified from it.

Rashi on Shabbat 95b:4:13.hebrew: ועדיין כלי הוא לקבל בו רימונים - שאם יחדו שוב לרימונים, מקבל טומאה מכאן ולהבא; או אם היה מיוחד לרימונים מתחילה, לא נטהר:
Rashi on Shabbat 95b:4:13.english: And it is still a vessel to hold pomegranates in it - For if he subsequently designated it for pomegranates, it is susceptible to ritual impurity from then on; or if it was designated for pomegranates from the outset, it did not become pure.

Rashi on Shabbat 95b:4:14.hebrew: טהור מכלום - משום כלי, אלא א"כ מצניעו לגיסטרא, יטמא בתורת גיסטרא:
Rashi on Shabbat 95b:4:14.english: Pure from anything - as a vessel, unless he sets it aside [to use] as a shard, [in which case] it becomes impure under the law of a shard.

Rashi on Shabbat 95b:4:15.hebrew: ואם היה מוקף צמיד פתיל - והוא באהל המת, אין טומאה נכנסת בו דרך נקב, ומצי על כל מה שבתוכו:
Rashi on Shabbat 95b:4:15.english: And if it was surrounded with a tight-fitting cover - and it is in the tent of a corpse, impurity does not enter it through a hole, and it protects all that is inside it.

Rashi on Shabbat 95b:4:16.hebrew: עד שיפחת רובו - דכל כלי פתוח כתיב (שם), דרך פתח נכנסת לו טומאה ולא דרך נקביו:
Rashi on Shabbat 95b:4:16.english: Until the majority of it is broken - For "every open vessel" is written (ibid.): impurity enters it through an opening, and not through its holes.

Rashi on Shabbat 95b:4:2.english: [Large enough] to let liquid out - A very fine hole through which liquid goes out.

Rashi on Shabbat 95b:4:3.hebrew: טהור מלטמא גיסטרא - כלומר, אם כלי שלם הוא, אינו נטהר בכך. אבל אם היה שבר כלי והיה ראוי להשתמש בו, דמקבל טומאה משנשבר — כדתנן: הן וקרקרותיהן ודופנותיהן יושבין שלא מסומכין כו', באלו טרפות (חולין דף נד:) — וניקב שוב כמוציא משקה, אינו טמא עוד משום תורת גיסטרא:
Rashi on Shabbat 95b:4:3.english: [It is] pure from becoming impure [as] a shard - That is to say, if it is a whole vessel, it does not become pure through this. However, if it was a broken piece of a vessel and was fit to be used — for it is susceptible to impurity [even] after it broke, as we learned in the Mishnah: "They, and their bottoms, and their sides, that sit without support, etc." in [the chapter] Eilu Tereifot (Chullin 54b) — and it was perforated again [with a hole large enough] to let liquid seep out, it is no longer impure under the law of a shard.

Rashi on Shabbat 95b:4:4.hebrew: גיסטרא - שבר כלי, ולקמיה מפרש טעמא דאין שבר כלי חשוב להצניעו משניקב, ולומר "הבא גיסטרא אחר ונניח תחתיו לקבל טיף טיף הנוטף מזה"; אבל אם היה כלי שלם וניקב מעט, אין מאבדין אותו, אלא אומר "הבא גיסטרא אחר ונניח תחתיו":
Rashi on Shabbat 95b:4:4.english: Gistera - A broken piece of a vessel, and later on [the Gemara] explains the reason: that a broken piece of a vessel is not significant enough to put away once it has been perforated, and to say, "Bring another shard and let us place it beneath it to catch the drops dripping from this one"; however, if it was a whole vessel and was slightly perforated, they do not discard it; rather, one says, "Bring another shard and let us place it beneath it."

Rashi on Shabbat 95b:4:5.hebrew: ועדיין כלי הוא לקדש בו מי חטאת - כלומר, אם כלי שלם היה וניקב כמוציא משקה, עדיין כל תורת כלי עליו, ואפי' לקדש בו מי חטאת באפר פרה, דבעינן כלי ראוי, דכתיב (במדבר יט) "מים חיים אל כלי", וכ"ש שמקבל טומאה:
Rashi on Shabbat 95b:4:5.english: And it is still a vessel in which to sanctify purification waters - That is to say, if it was a whole vessel and was perforated [with a hole large enough] for liquid to seep out, the full status of a vessel still applies to it — even to sanctify purification waters in it with the ashes of the [red] heifer, for we require a fit vessel, as it is written (Numbers 19): "living water in a vessel" — and all the more so that it can contract ritual impurity.

Rashi on Shabbat 95b:4:6.hebrew: ניקב ככונס משקה - שאם מושיבו על המים, נכנס בתוכו, דהיינו נקב רחב קצת:
Rashi on Shabbat 95b:4:6.english: Perforated [so as] to enable liquid to enter - For if one sets it upon water, [water] enters into it, which is a somewhat wide hole.

Rashi on Shabbat 95b:4:7.hebrew: טהור מלקדש בו מי חטאת - טהור לאו דוקא, אלא כמו טהר יומא (ברכות דף ב.), כלומר: בטל לו מתורת כלי לענין מי חטאת:
Rashi on Shabbat 95b:4:7.english: [It is] ritually pure in terms of sanctifying purification waters in it - 'Pure' is not [meant] literally; rather, [it is] like [the expression] 'taher yoma' ('the day passed') (Berakhot 2a), meaning, it has ceased [to have] the status of a vessel with respect to purification waters.

Rashi on Shabbat 95b:4:8.hebrew: ועדיין כלי הוא לענין הכשר זרעים - הזרועים בתוכו, דכתלושין נינהו, ואפילו לרבנן, שאין נקב זה ראוי להריח לחלוחית הקרקע:
Rashi on Shabbat 95b:4:8.english: And it is still a vessel with respect to rendering seeds susceptible [to impurity] - [Those seeds] that are sown inside it, for they are [considered] like detached [plants], and even according to the Rabbis, since this hole is not fit to absorb the moisture of the ground.

Rashi on Shabbat 95b:4:9.english: [If] it was perforated [the size of] a small root - [This] is larger than [a hole that] lets liquid enter.

Rashi on Shabbat 95b:5:1.hebrew: אלא במוקף צמיד פתיל - שאם ניקב כמוצא רימון, אינו מציל:
Rashi on Shabbat 95b:5:1.english: Only with [a vessel] surrounded by a sealed cover - For if it is punctured [to the size of] the outlet of a pomegranate, it does not protect [its contents].

Tosafot on Shabbat 95b:2:1.hebrew: ומודה ר"ש שאם ניקב בכדי טהרתו - פי' כמוציא זית, דסתמו של כלי חרס לאוכלין, ושיעורן כמוציא זית. ונראה לר"י דהיינו טעמא דמודה, משום דבטל אגב קרקע כשניקב בכדי טהרתו; ודוקא בניקב כמוציא זית, אבל בכלי המיוחד למשקין, אע"פ שטהרתו בכונס משקה, לא אמרי' דבטל, דאפי' לרבנן לא חשבי ליה כמחובר בכונס משקה, אלא כשורש קטן, כדאמר בסמוך:
Tosafot on Shabbat 95b:2:1.english: And Rabbi Shimon agrees that if it is perforated [with a hole] the size that renders it ritually pure - This means [a hole] large enough for an olive to pass through, for an ordinary earthenware vessel is [used] for food, and its measure [for ritual purity] is [a hole] large enough for an olive to pass through. And it appears to Rabbi Yitzchak that this is the reason he agrees: because it becomes nullified as part of the ground when it is perforated [with a hole] the size that renders it ritually pure. And this applies specifically when it is perforated [with a hole] large enough for an olive to pass through; however, in the case of a vessel designated for liquids, even though its [measure for] ritual purity is [a hole large enough] to let liquid in, we do not say that it becomes nullified, for even according to the Rabbis, they do not consider it attached [to the ground] with [a hole large enough] to let liquid in, but rather [only] with [a hole the size of] a small root, as [the Gemara] says shortly [below].

Tosafot on Shabbat 95b:4:1.hebrew: טהור מלקדש בו מי חטאת - וכ"ש דטהור מלקבל טומאה אם היה מיוחד למשקין:
Tosafot on Shabbat 95b:4:1.english: "It is ritually pure from sanctifying purification waters in it" - And all the more so that it is [ritually] pure from contracting ritual impurity if it was designated for liquids.

Tosafot on Shabbat 95b:4:2.hebrew: טהור מלהכשיר בו זרעים - משמע דכלי חרס בעי נקיבה, ודלא כפי' הקונט' בפ"ק דגיטין (דף ז.), שפירש דספינה של חרס — דכיון שהיא של עפר, חשובה כנקובה; ועת לקצר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 95b:4:2.english: It is ritually pure from rendering seeds in it capable [of becoming impure] - This implies that an earthenware vessel requires perforation [in order not to render seeds susceptible to impurity], unlike the explanation of the Kuntres [Rashi] in the first chapter of Gittin (7a), who explained regarding an earthenware boat that since it is made of earth, it is considered as if perforated — and it is a time to be brief.

Tosafot on Shabbat 95b:4:3.hebrew: ניקב כמוציא רימון טהור מכלום - תימה לר"י: היכי קאמר דטהור מכלום? והלא אם יחדו לגיסטרא מקבל טומאה, כדפי' בקונט'? וכפירושו ודאי כן הוא, שהרי אפילו אם נשברו בשברים דקים, מקבלים השברים טומאה בתורת גיסטרא, כשנשאר בשברים שיעור המפורש במסכת כלים (ס"ב משנה ב) ומייתי לה בפ' אלו טריפות (חולין נד:): "הדקים שבכלי חרס, הן וקרקרותיהן ודופנותיהן יושבין שלא מסומכין — שיעורן בכדי סיכת קטן עד לוג, ומלוג עד סאה ברביעית כו'". ועוד קשה לרשב"א, דהוה מצי למימר שש מדות בכלי חרס. וי"ל: דכשנשבר לגמרי, השברים ראויין לגיסטרא; אבל כשהכלי שלם, אלא שניקב כמוציא רימון, אין ראוי לגיסטרא, ואפי' יחדו — בטלה דעתו אצל כל אדם. אבל מתוך פי' הקונט' משמע דכשניקב כמוציא רימון ראוי הוא לגיסטרא, דפירש: טהור מכלום משום כלי, אא"כ מצניעו משום גיסטרא. ולפירושו, הא דלא נקט ו' מדות — דלא מיירי אלא כשיכול להשתמש כדרכן, וניקב כמוציא רימון אין ראוי אלא אם כן מטהו על צידו:
Tosafot on Shabbat 95b:4:3.english: "[If] it was perforated [with a hole large enough] to enable a pomegranate to go out, it is ritually pure from any [type of impurity]." - R"I [Rabbeinu Yitzchak] wonders: How can [the Gemara] say that it is ritually pure from any [type of impurity]? Surely, if one designated it [for use] as a shard [gistera], it can contract impurity, as Rashi explained! And according to his explanation, it is certainly so, for even if [earthenware vessels] are broken into small shards, the shards can contract impurity under the law of a gistera, provided there remains in the shards the measure specified in Tractate Kelim (ch. 2, mishnah 2), which is cited in the chapter [entitled] Eilu Tereifot (Chullin 54b): "The small earthenware vessels — they, their bottoms, and their sides that sit without being propped up — their measure is [enough oil] to anoint a small child, [for vessels] up to a log; and from a log up to a se'ah, a revi'it, etc." Furthermore, Rashba raises a difficulty: [The Gemara] could have stated "six measures in an earthenware vessel." And one can answer that when it is completely broken, the shards are fit [to be used] as a gistera; however, when the vessel is whole except that it was perforated [with a hole large enough] to enable a pomegranate to go out, it is not fit [to be used] as a gistera, and even if one designated it [for that], his intention is nullified [as eccentric] in the view of all people. However, from Rashi's commentary it is implied that when it is perforated [with a hole large enough] to enable a pomegranate to go out, it is fit [to be used] as a gistera, for he explained: "[It is] ritually pure from any [impurity]" as a vessel, unless he puts it away [for use] as a gistera. And according to his explanation, the reason [the Gemara] did not mention six measures is that it is speaking only of when one can use [the vessels] in their normal manner, whereas [when] it is perforated [with a hole large enough] to enable a pomegranate to go out, it is not fit [for use] unless one tilts it on its side.

Tosafot on Shabbat 95b:5:1.hebrew: שמא לא שמעת אלא במוקף צמיד פתיל - תימה לר"י: דילמא במיוחד לרימונים שמע, ואצטריך לאפוקי מדר"א דאמר בסמוך ניקב כמוציא זית אין לו טומאה כו'. וי"ל דמשמע דבסתם כלי חרס איירי, בלא יחוד. וליכא למימר דלענין הכשר זרעים שמע, כמ"ד בסמוך שיעורו כמוציא רימון — לפירש הקונט' דפירש דלענין הכשר זרעים פליגי — דא"כ, אמאי נקט כלי חרס? אפי' כלי עץ נמי! ועוד, דרבא סבירא ליה דלענין הכשר זרעים שיעורו כשורש קטן:
Tosafot on Shabbat 95b:5:1.english: "Perhaps you only heard [this] when [it is] surrounded by a sealed cover" - R"I finds this difficult: Perhaps [Rav Asi] heard [this] regarding [a vessel] designated for pomegranates, and it was necessary [to state this] to exclude [the view of] Rabbi Eliezer, who says just below [that if] it is perforated [with a hole large enough] to enable an olive to go out, it has no impurity, etc. And one can answer that it is implied that [Rav Asi] is speaking of an ordinary earthenware vessel, without designation. And one cannot say that he heard [it] with regard to rendering seeds susceptible [to impurity], like the one who says just below [that] its measure is [a hole large enough] to enable a pomegranate to go out — according to the explanation of the Kuntres [Rashi], who explained that they disagree with regard to rendering seeds susceptible [to impurity] — for if so, why did he specify an earthenware vessel? Even a wooden vessel [would have] the same [law]! And furthermore, Rava holds that with regard to rendering seeds susceptible [to impurity], its measure is [the size of] a small root.
